items.title: 63520_Ernie Fields oral history interview
items.q: He said, I'm a carpenter but I can play a horn, and I said I can too. So he said we got to get together then and I said yeah.

ctx.x: And so, I just walked in a while and talked to them and said, when do you rehearse and they went on to tell me about their schedule and they said, do you play? And I told them I play a trombone and they said, how come you don't come here and sing with us sometime? And so I said well I will.

I would just like to mention something before--that's just the beginning of my first being around a band, but a very important thing I'd like to say, while I was doing the gig with Ball and the gig with Thomas it was getting around that there was some youngster in town that plays a pretty good trombone. So, Butterbeans and Susie came to town and Eddie
Heyward Sr. was in charge of the band, and he wanted to augment the band. He was going to be in the Dixie Theatre for two weeks and this is on the TOBA*circuit--

items.title: 63520_Ernie Fields oral history interview
items.q: as time went on we became kind of buddy-buddy

ctx.x: didn't know there were but three kinds of shoes, that is, white shoes, black shoes and tan shoes, but still, I'm going to work in one of them shine parlors.

One day I was shining a man's shoes, he had on tan shoes, and I was just shining the heels, I was going to make them shine like the toe, and all the boys that worked there, they began to laugh, and they would say little words, this and that, and I didn't know what they were talking about, so when they got through and the man handed me a nickel, and everybody fell out laughing, and all but one boy, and that boy was Walter Thomas. He said, we tried to tell you, and the guys would say, you're lucky, you got a…

days, and so I thanked him and as time went on we became kind of buddy-buddy and he says maybe Saturday we're going to do this and I'd say, no, I'm saving my money. He say, what are you so tight for; I'd say I'm trying to save money to go to Tuskegee. And he said, that's what I'm working for, I'm going to some school up in Topeka, training school. He said that's where I'm going to school.
